signal.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models
signal.summary: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。

editorial.intro: 这项研究围绕视觉—语言—动作模型展开，关注机器人如何把视觉观察和语言指令，持续转换成跨时间的动作，而不是只对当前画面做一次反应。
editorial.why_it_matters: VLA 的记忆、推理和实时执行能力，直接决定具身智能能否从演示动作走向长时任务和真实部署。
editorial.watch_next: 继续核对实验是否覆盖真实机器人、长时任务和跨场景泛化。

evidence.title: RoboHarness: A Simple Harness Outperforms VLA and World Actions Models
evidence.excerpt: The rise of large language models (LLMs) has opened a path toward generalist embodied AI, raising the question of how LLMs can act in the physical world. One straightforward approach is training the model to generate actions: collect robot-action data and video demonstration, refine LLM architecture with an action head, and train a vision-language-action (VLA) model at scale. However, we argue that coding agents have the potential to realize generalist embodied manipulation. All they need is a simple yet effective robot harness. We present RoboHarness: a robotic harness that gives LLM agents a visual-geometric control panel so that they can directly understand and invoke embodied tasks. With RoboHarness, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next outperforms state-of-the-art VLA models on BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025 tasks. The implementation will be released as open source.
